questions.question: If 2x + 5y = 15 and xy = 6, then the value of 4x² + 25y² is ________.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

2x + 5y = 15

and xy = 6

**Formula used:**

(A + B)² = A² + B² + 2AB

**Calculation:**

⇒ 2x + 5y = 15

Squaring both sides

⇒ (2x + 5y)² = 15²

⇒ 4x² + 25y² + 2 × 2x × 5y = 225

⇒ 4x² + 25y² + 20xy = 225

Putting the value of xy = 6

⇒ 4x2 + 25y2 + (20 × 6) = 225

⇒ 4x² + 25y² = 225 - 120

⇒ 4x2 + 25y2 = 105

**∴ The correct answer is 105.**

questions.question: A number first increased by 8% and then decreased by 3% to get 2619. What is 5% of that number?
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

If a number is increased by P% then,

N = N × (100 + P)%

If a number is decreased by P% then,

N = N × (100 - P)%

**Calculation:**

Let the number be N.

According to the question:

⇒ N × 108% × 97% = 2619

⇒ N = (2619 × 100 × 100)/(108 × 97)

⇒ N = 25 × 100 = 2500

Now, 

⇒ 2500 × 5% = 125

**∴ The correct answer is 125.**

questions.question: The sides of a triangle are 20 cm, 21 cm and 29 cm. The area of the triangle formed by joining the mid points of the sides of triangle will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

ABC is a triangle.

AB = 20 cm; BC = 21 cm ; AC = 29 cm

D, E, and F are the midpoints of AB, BC and AC respectively.

**Concept used:**

The line segment joining the midpoint of any two sides of the triangle is parallel 

and half of the length of the third side.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/336b0fbcf468ead50ce800559bc91806dc6bfa66786208fa1cdd03254cbc2320.png] 

In the figure, D, E, and F are the midpoints of AB, BC and AC respectively.

From the midpoint theorem:

DE = 21/2 = 10.5 cm ; EF = 20/2 = 10 cm ; DF = 29/2 = 14.5 cm

Semi - perimeter (S) = (DE + EF + DF)/2

⇒ (10.5 + 10 + 14.5)/2

⇒ 35/2 = 17.5 cm

Area of triangle = √{S(S - DE) × (S - EF) × (S - DF)}

⇒ √{17.5 × (17.5 - 10.5) × (17.5 - 10) × (17.5 - 14.5)}

⇒ √{17.5 × 7 × 7.5 × 3}

⇒ √2756.25 = 52.5 = 52 (1)/(2) cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 52 (1)/(2) cm2.**** **

questions.solution:

questions.question: If the triangles ABC and PQR are similar and if ∠A = 35°, ∠B = 65° then ∠R = __________.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

△ ABC ∼ △PQR

∠A = 35°, ∠B = 65° 

**Concept used:**

The sum of all three angles = 180° 

**Calculation:**

In △ ABC

∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 35 + 65 + ∠C = 180°

⇒ ∠C = 180 - (35 + 65)

⇒ ∠C = 180° - 100 = 80°

Since △ ABC ∼ △PQR then,

∠C = ∠R = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

questions.question: A rides his bicycle at 15 km/h, while B starts his ride after 6 hours to catch A with a speed of 25 km/h. Time taken by B to catch A (in hours) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Lead distance created by **A** = 15 × 6 = 90 km.

Relative speed (same direction) = 25 − 15 = 10 km/h.

Time taken by **B** to catch **A** = Lead Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 90 ÷ 10 = 9 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of **A** = 15 km/h

Speed of **B** = 25 km/h

Time gap = 6 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b10ee40206aa5707bf5b081aec046c03eb08e156c4f7477a99189f6968a0ee55.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered by **A** in 6 hours = 15 × 6 = 90 km

⇒ When **B** starts, the distance between **A** and **B** is 90 km.

⇒ Relative speed of **B** relative to **A** = 25 − 15 = 10 km/h

⇒ Time taken by **B** to cover the gap = 90 ÷ 10

⇒ Time taken = 9 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 9 hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects move in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂).

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move toward each other, the relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Meeting Time Rule

The time required for a faster object to catch a slower object is given by: Meeting Time = (Initial separation distance) ÷ (Relative Speed).</p

questions.question: Evaluate the given expression: cos² 36° + cos 54° ⋅ sin 36° + (frac{tan 26circ}{cot 64circ})
questions.solution:
**Formula used:**

Tan (90° - θ) = cot θ

Cos (90° - θ) = sin θ 

**Calculation:**

cos2 36° + cos 54° ⋅ sin 36° + (frac{tan 26circ}{cot 64circ})

⇒ cos2 36° + cos 54° ⋅ sin 36° + (tan 26°/cot 64°)

⇒ cos2 36° + cos (90° - 36) ⋅ sin 36° + tan 26°/cot (90° - 26)

⇒ cos2 36° + sin 36° ⋅ sin 36° + tan 26°/tan 26°

⇒ cos2 36° + sin² 36° + 1

⇒ 1 + 1 = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

questions.question: The chord of a circle is equal to its radius. The angle (in degrees) subtended by this chord at any point on the minor arc of the circle is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The chords of a circle = radius of the circle

**Concept used:**

The angle of an equilateral triangle = 60°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/be2bdeec80d53e4a8ce034529d6fb1351816e3b4c859c64d2ad2b4584cf14852.png] 

In the figure:

OD = OE = radius

DE = OD = OE

So, △DOE is an equilateral triangle.

∠DOE = 60°

⇒ ∠DQE = (∠DOE/2)

⇒ 60/2 = 30°

DQEP is a cyclic quadrilateral.

∠DQE + ∠DPE = 180°

⇒ 30 + ∠DPE = 180

⇒ ∠DPE = 180 - 30

⇒ ∠DPE = 150°

questions.question: A manufacturer marked an item at ₹75 and sold it allowing a 14% discount. If his profit was 29%, then the cost price (in ₹) of the item was:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked price (M.P) = Rs.75

Discount% = 14%

Profit% = 29%

**Formula used:**

C.P/M.P = (100 - D)%/(100 + P)%

Where, C.P = cost price ; D = discount

and P = profit 

**Calculation:**

⇒ C.P/M.P = (100 - D)%/(100 + P)%

⇒ C.P/75 = (100 - 14)/(100 + 29)

⇒ C.P = (86 × 75)/129

⇒ C.P = 2 × 25 = 50

∴ The correct answer is 50.

questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠M = 90°

**Concept used:**

In right-angled triangle:

H² = P² + B²

Sec θ = B/H

Where, H = hypotenuse

P = perpendicular ; B = base

questions.question: What is the difference between the compound interest on ₹6,400 for 1 year at 5% per annum compounded yearly and half-yearly?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs.6400

Time = 1 year and rate = 5%

**Concept used:**

Compound interest (C.I) = P × Effective rate%

Effective rate% for 2 years = R₁ + R₂ + (R₁ × R₂)/100

**Calculation:**

For compounded annually:

C.I = 6400 × 5% = 320

For compounded half-yearly:

New rate = 5/2% = 2.5%

Time = 1 × 2 = 2 years

Effective rate% for 2 years = 2.5 + 2.5 + (2.5)²/100

⇒ 5 + 0.0625 = 5.0625%

C.I = 6400 × 5.0625% = Rs.324

Required difference = 324 - 320 = Rs.4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

questions.question: The perimeter of a sector of a circle of radius 7.4 cm is 20.6 cm. The area of this sector is:
questions.solution:

Radius of circle = 7.4 cm

Perimeter of a sector = 20.6 cm

**Formula used:**

Perimeter of sector = 2r + (2 × π × r × θ)/360°

Area of a sector = (π × r² × θ)/360°

**Calculation:**

Perimeter of sector = 2r + (2 × π × r × θ)/360°

⇒ 20.6 = 2 × 7.4 + (2 × π × 7.4 × θ)/360°

⇒ 20.6 - 14.8 = (2 × π × 7.4 × θ)/360°

questions.question: If A = 60° and B = 30°, find the value of ((tan A-tan B))/((1+tan A tan B)).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The given expression is the direct expansion of the trigonometric identity for tan(A − B).

⇒ tan(A − B) = (tan A − tan B) ÷ (1 + tan A × tan B)

Substitute A = 60° and B = 30°:

⇒ tan(60° − 30°) = tan 30°

⇒ tan 30° = 1/√3

**∴ The correct answer is 1/√3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A = 60°

B = 30°

**Formula Used:**

Direct substitution of standard trigonometric values.

tan 60° = √3

tan 30° = 1/√3

**Calculations:**

Substitute the exact values into the expression:

⇒ Expression = (tan 60° − tan 30°) ÷ (1 + tan 60° × tan 30°)

⇒ Numerator = √3 − 1/√3

⇒ Numerator = (3 − 1) ÷ √3 = 2/√3

⇒ Denominator = 1 + (√3 × 1/√3)

⇒ Denominator = 1 + 1 = 2

⇒ Expression value = (2/√3) ÷ 2

⇒ Expression value = 1/√3

**∴ The correct answer is 1/√3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Angle Formula for Addition

tan(A + B) = (tan A + tan B) ÷ (1 − tan A × tan B). This formula is used when adding two compound angles.

Double Angle Formula for Tangent

tan(2A) = (2 × tan A) ÷ (1 − tan² A). This is directly derived by substituting B = A in the addition formula.

Standard Tangent Values

tan 0° = 0, tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3, tan 90° = Not Defined.
</p

questions.question: George can do 35% of the total work in 6 days. Jim and George together completed a piece of work in 12 days. In how many days could Jim, working alone, complete the entire task?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**George** completes 100% work in 6 × (100 / 35) = 120/7 days.

Total Work (LCM of 120/7 and 12) = 120 units.

Efficiency of **George** = 7 and Efficiency of (**Jim** + **George**) = 10.

Efficiency of **Jim** = 10 − 7 = 3 units/day.

Time taken by **Jim** = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Work done by **George** = 35% in 6 days.

Time taken by **Jim** and **George** together = 12 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken by **George** to complete 100% work = 6 ÷ 0.35 = 600/35 = 120/7 days.

⇒ Let the total work be the **LCM** of 120/7 and 12, which is 120 units.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 **George**
 120/7
 120
 7
 
 

 **Jim + George**
 12
 10
 
 

⇒ Efficiency of **Jim** = Efficiency of (**Jim** + **George**) − Efficiency of **George**

⇒ Efficiency of **Jim** = 10 − 7 = 3 units/day.

⇒ Time taken by **Jim** alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of **Jim**

⇒ Time taken by **Jim** = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task. If the ratio of time taken by A and B is x:y, then the ratio of their efficiencies is y:x.

Combined Work Rate

If person A takes 'a' days and person B takes 'b' days to complete a task individually, they will complete it together in (a × b) / (a + b) days.

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed among workers in the ratio of the total work done by each, which is the product of their individual efficiency and the time they worked.</p

questions.question: If one diagonal of a rhombus is equal to its side, then the diagonals of the rhombus are in the ratio of:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

One diagonal of a rhombus is equal to its side.

**Concept used:**

All sides of a rhombus are equal.

Diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at 90°.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/521eeacb6ef778c40d31df3edf49c7db733aa9455e49ac144100fcf5a15ec312.png] 

Let the side of the rhombus be A.

⇒ CD = AC = A

In ΔDOC,

⇒ CD² = OC² + OD²

⇒ A² = (A/2)² + OD²

⇒ OD² = A² − A²/4

⇒ OD² = (4A² − A²)/4

⇒ OD = √(3A²/4)

⇒ OD = (√3A)/2

Now,

⇒ BD = OD + OB

⇒ BD = (√3A)/2 + (√3A)/2

⇒ BD = √3A

Required ratio = AC : BD

⇒ A : √3A

⇒ 1 : √3

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: The cost of 12 apples and 15 oranges is ₹660. The cost of 15 apples and 21 oranges is ₹870. Find the cost of one apple.
questions.solution:

12 apples + 15 oranges = Rs.660

15 apples + 21 oranges = Rs.870

**Calculation:**

Let the cost of an apple = x

the cost of an orange = y

According to the question:

⇒ 12x + 15y = 660

⇒ 15y = 660 - 12x

⇒ y = (660 - 12x)/15 ------ (1)

Now,

⇒ 15x + 21y = 870

Putting the value of y in the equation

⇒ 15x + {21 × (660 - 12x)/15} = 870

⇒ 15x + {7 × (660 - 12x)/5} = 870

⇒ 75x + {7 × (660 - 12x)} = 870 × 5

⇒ 75x + 4620 - 84x = 4350

⇒ - 9x = - 270

⇒ x = Rs.30

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.30.**
